sql.title: {title} · table SQL · analysis v{v}
sql.env_none_note: If an environment without a record already has an earlier version, tell the AI which one (line 1 of that file) instead of adding sections 1-4.
sql.env_at: {env}  at v{n}  → needs only section 5, "v{n} → v{v}"
sql.env_same: {env}  at v{n}  → nothing changed since v{n}; needs nothing
sql.env_done: {env}  at v{n}  → up to date; needs nothing
sql.after_run: Once an environment has v{v} (however it got there), tell the AI so it records it; next time only what is missing is listed.
sql.rollback_note: Section 6 is the rollback; do not run it normally.
sql.s3: Section 3  Initial rows of new tables
sql.s4: Section 4  Changes to existing rows (after sections 1 and 2)
sql.s5: Section 5  Catch-up: only for environments that have an earlier version; one with none takes sections 1-4
sql.s6: Section 6  Rollback: do not run normally
sql.check: Check afterwards; the result should be above 0:
sql.since_whole: : added after v{n}; run the full statement
sql.gone: {name} ({title}): dropped from the requirement after v{n}. Ask whether to drop it where it exists and do that by hand; there is no DROP here.
sql.rb_how: To roll back, use the statements between /* and */, top to bottom.
sql.rb_order: The order is the reverse of the release: data first, then table changes, then new tables.
sql.rb_drop: Drop the new table: {name} (its rows go with it)
sql.rb_manual: The analysis has no rollback for this; undo it by hand.

release.hold_p: Everything else goes out as usual. Release these once the question is settled and the analysis updated.
release.before_p: Each step says what must be true and how to check it. Handing it to an AI is easiest; doing it yourself, tick each step as you go. Names and values in grey copy with one click.
release.deploy_p: Deploy once everything before it is done.
release.after_p: Watch these once it is live; if something is wrong, roll back as below.
release.rollback_p: Fastest first; try them from the top.
release.reset_confirm: Click again to clear ticks for {env}
release.sql_fresh: {env}'s tables and data have this change: sections 1-4 of {file}
release.sql_catch: {env} is at v{from} and needs the “v{from} → v{v}” group in section 5 of {file}
release.sql_done: Tables and data are fine: {env} is already at v{from}
release.sql_same: Tables and data are fine: nothing changed since v{from}
release.sql_verify: The new tables and columns exist, and applying the change raised no errors.
release.sql_check: Then check the data change; the result should be above 0:
release.tell: In place? Send this to the AI so it records it:
release.tell_text: {title} ({id}): {env}'s tables are now at v{v}; please record it.
release.copy_failed: Could not copy automatically. The text is selected: press Ctrl+C
release.sql_back: Undo the table and data changes: section 6 of {file}
release.sql_back_d: Rarely needed: new tables and columns do no harm to the old version. Use it only if data went wrong.
release.caveat: The list says what each step must reach and how to check it; how to get there is up to the tools at hand or the person doing it. Ticks stay in this browser on this computer. Once the tables are in place, tell the AI the version: only then do the SQL file and this page know what that environment still needs.
release.ai_p: Send this to an AI that can act (with tools that submit SQL, change configs, deploy). It works through the list for {env}, checks each step, and asks you before changing anything.
release.ai_text: Following the release checklist of {title} ({id}), bring {env} up to date: do each step with the tools you have, check it as the step says, and record the table version when done. Ask me before changing {env}.
